columns.headline: Joe G and Brad Break an 11-11 Tie While Heading Opposite Directions
columns.dek: The all-time series is dead even, one of them has won five straight and the other has lost five straight, and ESPN still calls it a near coin flip.
body: The game of the week is Joe G against Brad, because the all-time series is tied 11-11 and somebody finally gets to stop saying it is tied. ESPN projects Joe G for 102.49 and Brad for 99.40, a 3.09-point gap and a 52% to 48% split. Joe G is third at 15-7 on a W5 streak with a 99.13% playoff chance. Brad is 11th at 7-15 on an L5 streak with a 0.98% playoff chance. Brad is even projected above the 98.52 median, which is nice for a team that has spent five straight weeks losing anyway. If Brad wins, he gets the series lead and nothing else. If he loses, he gets a sixth straight loss and a rivalry he can no longer call even.

The closest projection on the board is Flanders against Kris: 98.74 to 98.30, a 0.44-point gap, 50% each. Flanders is ninth at 9-13 on a W2 streak with an 18.63% playoff chance and leads the series 10-6. Kris is fourth at 13-9, tied on record with Ben and ahead of him on points, yet ESPN gives Ben the better playoff chance, 90.68% to 84.93%. Kris has the higher seat and the worse odds, which is the fantasy equivalent of a corner office with no window.

The biggest mismatch is Jon against Joe K. Jon is projected for 126.41, Joe K for 83.49, a 42.92-point gap and a 22% win chance for Joe K. Joe K is sixth at 11-11 with a 29.45% playoff chance, tied on record with Jeff, who sits seventh and somehow has better odds at 48.15%. Joe K brings a W1 streak into this, the shortest heater a man can have, and ESPN looked at it and shrugged. Jon leads the series 5-4 and is second at 15-7, tied on record with Joe G and ahead on points.

Chad is alone in first at 18-4, rides a W5 streak, owns a 100% playoff chance and carries the top projection of the week, 127.88, into a 73% win chance against Collin's 92.11. And yet Collin leads that series 7-5. Collin is 10th at 7-15, tied with Brad and ahead of him on points, but with a 0.85% playoff chance, lower than Brad's.

Jared is alone in last at 3-19, has lost seven straight, has no playoff chance at all and gets the lowest projection on the slate, 74.42. TJ, on an L4 streak himself, is a 61% favorite at 89.67 and leads the series 7-1. Two teams that have forgotten how to win, and one of them is legally required to. Ben is also a 61% favorite, 112.24 to Jeff's 94.48, even though Jeff leads that series 9-7.

Secret Santa: the buy-by date was November 20, and seven managers are still at the North Pole without a shirt picked, including Chad, who has a 100% playoff chance and no shirt. Brad, Ben, Collin, Jared, Jeff and Joe K are right there with him. Nobody has wrapped anything. Projections are ESPN's; the shame is all yours.

columns.headline: Chad and Kris Meet in a Coin Flip at the Top of the Table
columns.dek: ESPN gives first-place Chad a 51% chance against Kris. Jared is projected for 49.33, and nine managers still have not picked a Secret Santa shirt.
body: The game of the week is Kris against Chad, and ESPN can barely tell them apart. Chad is projected for 107.37, Kris for 105.15, a gap of 2.22 that makes it the closest projection on the slate, with win chances of 51% and 49%. Chad sits first at 16-4 on a W4 streak with 1231.76 points and a 99.95% playoff chance, about as close to a lock as you can get without being good on Sunday. Kris is third at 13-7, tied on record with Jon and Joe G, and trails the series 9-5. A win here does not make Kris the best team in the league. It just hands Chad a fifth loss to think about.

Meanwhile, big brother Joe G, the one who is supposed to know better, rides his own W4 streak into a projection of 86.77, below the projected median of 95.66. Flanders, at 8-12 and ninth, is projected for 95.56 and gets a 56% win chance, and Flanders leads the series 10-7. Little brother is in the game of the week. Big brother is a 44% underdog to a team with an 18.25% playoff chance.

The biggest mismatch is Collin against Jared, and it is not close on paper: a projected gap of 44.37. Jared, last at 3-17 on an L6 streak, is projected for 49.33, a number that looks less like a lineup and more like a cry for help. His playoff chance is 0.1%. Collin gets 80% odds and leads the series 8-3, which is the only thing going right for an 11th-place team with a 1.88% playoff chance. Eleventh against twelfth, and somebody still has to win it.

Brad brings an L4 streak, a 7-13 record and a 5.35% playoff chance into a projection of 98.19 against Jon's 118.31, the top projection of the week. ESPN has Jon at 62%. Brad leads the series 6-1, which is the one stat line on his page he would want framed.

Then there is the 10-10 traffic jam. TJ is sixth with a 43.33% playoff chance, Joe K seventh at 25.45%, Jeff eighth at 50.05%, so the model likes the guy ranked lowest of the three best. TJ, on an L3 streak, is projected for 81.76 against Jeff's 95.75 and leads that series 4-1. Joe K gets the second-lowest projection of the week, 79.25, against Ben's 115.68, and a 28% win chance. Joe K leads the series 10-5. ESPN does not care.

Secret Santa shirts are due Friday, and nine managers are still at the North Pole without a shirt picked, including Chad, who has nearly clinched a playoff spot and has not clinched a gift. Only Flanders, Kris and TJ have ordered one. Nobody has wrapped anything. The league that cannot set a lineup also cannot shop.

columns.headline: Joe K Loses by 0.24 With the Fix Sitting on His Bench
columns.dek: Jon drops the week's high score on Brad, Ben steals one by 0.24, and the brothers both win, though only one of them set his lineup like an adult.
body: The game of the week was decided by a rounding error and a bad decision. Ben beat Joe K 96.10 to 95.86, a margin of 0.24, and Joe K is the only loser this week whose best lineup would have won. He left Braelon Allen and his 8.90 on the bench to start Emari Demercado in the flex, and Demercado returned 3.90. His best lineup was 100.86. That is not bad luck, that is dumb, the kind of dumb that leaves a man staring at his phone at midnight wondering how he lost to a team whose stud got lapped by his own projection.

Because Ben did not exactly earn it either. Ja'Marr Chase was projected for 21.02 and gave him 5.60, the worst start against projection of anyone this week. Ladd McConkey bailed him out with 18.20, and Ben walks away a winner while still trailing the series to Joe K 10-6. Joe K somehow moved up a spot to sixth at 11-11, which tells you everything about the bottom half of this league.

Jon put up the high score, 145.40, and spent it on Brad, who managed 67.46. The 77.94 margin was the biggest of the week. Dak Prescott threw in 35.90 and Jonah Coleman ran for 32.90 against a projection of 17.81, the best start of the week. Even with Hunter Henry laying a donut at tight end, Jon still had more than he needed, which is a lot of production for once matched by the product. Brad still leads the series 6-2, a fact he will cling to like it means anything.

Brad's afternoon: Jonathan Taylor gave him 4.70 on a projection of 15.17 and Emeka Egbuka chipped in 2.80. His best lineup was 75.46, so this one was not a lineup problem, it was a roster problem. He slid to 11th at 7-15. Brad would like everyone to know his head is not that big, and this week neither was his score.

Jared had the low score at 57.32, and his best possible lineup, 64.52, would also have lost to Collin. Matthew Stafford put up a donut at quarterback and DK Metcalf managed 0.70. Jared is 3-19 and alone in last. Collin won that game with 77.68, still under the 88.20 median, after benching Khalil Shakir and his 12.80 to start Kyle Monangai, who scored 1.80. Collin leads that series 9-3 and climbed to 10th, ahead of Brad on rank at the same 7-15.

TJ started Aaron Rodgers, projected for 15.11, and got a donut. The 65.40 that followed lost to Jeff and dropped TJ two spots to eighth. Jeff won with 82.96, below the median, while Courtland Sutton laid a donut at receiver and Antonio Williams posted 16.70 on his bench. Mike Evans saved him with 19.90 on a projection of 9.47.

Chad beat Kris 103.64 to 78.26 and left nothing on his bench, a perfect lineup, with Travis Kelce posting 22.40 on a 9.49 projection. Big brother Joe G also won, 112.70 to 93.44 over Flanders, but benched Kayshon Boutte's 11.00 to start Chase Brown, who gave him 6.10. Joe G is the one who is supposed to know better. Chad sits alone in first at 18-4; Joe G rose to third, tied with Jon at 15-7 and behind him on points. Meanwhile, Secret Santa: the shirts were due November 20, nothing is wrapped, and seven managers, Chad included, are still at the North Pole without a shirt picked.

columns.headline: Kris and Joe G Settle a 7-7 Series With Second Place in View
columns.dek: Second against fourth, a series dead even at 7-7, and ESPN picking Kris. Elsewhere, Chad gets Jared and Joe K gets a projection that reads like a cry for help.
body: The game of the week is Kris against Joe G, because it is second against fourth, both of them in the playoff picture, and the all-time series is tied 7-7. Somebody walks out of Sunday owning this rivalry and the other one walks out with a story about how it was actually close. ESPN has Kris at 107.01 and Joe G at 87.62, a 19.39-point gap and a 62% to 38% split. Joe G has won three straight and Kris lost last week, so the hot team is the underdog, which is the most Joe G sentence ever written.

The stakes are real. Kris is second at 12-6 with an 89.28% playoff chance. Joe G is fourth at 11-7, tied on record with Jon, who sits third because he has more points. Joe G somehow has the better playoff odds of the two, 81.08% to Jon's 79.18%, so ESPN trusts him more than the standings do. Lose this one and he is a guy with a three-game streak and nothing to show for it.

The closest projection on the board is Jeff against Collin: 92.13 to 95.34, a 3.21-point gap and a 48% to 52% split. Jeff has lost three straight and is eighth at 8-10. Collin has won two straight and is eleventh at 6-12 with a 6.9% playoff chance, which is a two-game heater in service of nothing. Jeff leads the series 7-6. ESPN has the eleventh-place team favored over him, and nobody even had to be mean about it.

The biggest mismatch is Chad against Jared. Chad is alone in first at 14-4 with a 99.75% playoff chance and is projected for 110.44. Jared is alone in last at 3-15, has lost five straight, holds a 0.2% playoff chance and is projected for 57.34, the lowest number on the board by a mile, a 53.1-point gap and an 18% win chance. And yet Jared leads this series 11-9. Whatever Jared has on Chad, he should use it this week, because his lineup is not going to.

Joe K against TJ is the other blowout on paper: TJ at 111.97, the top projection of the week, against Joe K at 71.47, a 40.5-point gap and a 25% win chance for Joe K. Joe K has won three straight and is still seventh at 9-9 with a 28.93% playoff chance, lower than Jeff's 34.28% at 8-10. That is ESPN looking at a .500 team on a heater and saying no thanks. TJ has lost two straight and is fifth at 10-8, ahead of Ben on points. The series is tied 4-4, so one of these two geniuses gets the bragging rights.

Ben and Brad are a near coin flip at 98.17 to 102.87, 47% to 53%, with the series tied 8-8. Brad has lost three straight and is ninth at 7-11 with a 19.5% playoff chance, tied on record with Flanders and somehow behind him in the odds. Jon is a 65% favorite over Flanders, 108.74 to 84.38, even though Flanders leads that series 3-2.

columns.headline: Flanders Drops 143.32, Loses Anyway, and TJ Benches His Way Out
columns.dek: Jon edges Flanders in the closest game of the week, Chad flattens Jared, and two managers lose games their own benches would have won.
body: Flanders put up 143.32, the second-best score of the week, and lost to the only number bigger: Jon's 148.52. The 5.20-point margin was the closest game of the week, and Flanders paid for it in the flex, where Devin Singletary put up a donut while Kaelon Black sat on the bench with 13.60. The best lineup on that roster was 155.92, enough to win. George Pickens scored 38.00 on a 9.89 projection, the best start of the week against projection, and Christian McCaffrey added 44.30, so two players went nuclear and the manager still found a way to lose. The series is tied 3-3.

Jon will take it. Dak Prescott scored 34.42 on a 16.55 projection, Tyler Higbee laid a donut at tight end, and the week's high score lifted Jon from third to second at 13-7. Big budget, one blank frame, and for once the production actually cleared the box office. Jon, Kris and Joe G are all 13-7, with Jon ahead on points.

The biggest beating was Chad over Jared, 120.58 to 85.36, a 35.22-point margin. Jahmyr Gibbs scored 40.70 on a 21.63 projection, which paid for Kyren Williams scoring 4.20 on a 16.97 projection. Chad sits alone in first at 16-4. Jared, alone in last at 3-17, got 1.40 from Tyler Warren at tight end, and even the best lineup on the roster, 100.06, loses to Chad. Jared still leads the series 11-10, which is the kind of stat you frame when it is all you have.

Then there is TJ, the other manager who lost by choice. Drake Maye started at quarterback and scored 3.02 on a 21.97 projection while Aaron Rodgers sat on the bench with 15.62. TJ's best lineup was 106.78, more than enough to beat Joe K's 98.52. That is dumb, not a little dumb, the kind of dumb that leaves 19.96 points on the pine. TJ slides from fifth to sixth at 10-10, and Joe K leads the series 5-4.

Joe K, for once, did nothing wrong and still got punished. Joe K left nothing on the bench, a perfect lineup, and it came up 1.51 short of the 100.03 median. Patrick Mahomes scored 35.42 on an 18.55 projection, Tucker Kraft scored 2.40, and Joe K went 1-1 to stay seventh at 10-10. Acing the test and still failing the class is a very Joe K way to spend a Sunday.

Joe G beat Kris 123.06 to 101.54 behind Brock Purdy's 31.66 and Chase Brown's 24.30, despite a donut from Kayshon Boutte in the flex. Kris cleared the median by 1.51 and still dropped from second to third, with Rhamondre Stevenson scoring 1.00 on an 11.78 projection next to Chuba Hubbard's 31.70. Joe G leads that series 8-7. Jeff beat Collin 102.04 to 73.48, the low score of the week, and Collin's best lineup of 89.70 still loses, so leaving Omarion Hampton's 17.00 on the bench was just garnish. Jeff leads that series 8-6.

Ben beat Brad 91.06 to 80.10 in a game where both missed the median. Bryce Young scored 8.10 on an 18.80 projection, Brad's best lineup was 83.70, and Brad falls to tenth at 7-13 as Flanders climbs past to ninth. Ben moves up to fifth and takes a 9-8 series lead despite Brock Bowers scoring 2.80. Secret Santa check: ten managers are still at the North Pole with no shirt picked, Flanders has ordered, TJ has picked one, nobody has wrapped anything, and the shirts are due November 20.

columns.headline: Joe G and Jon Fight Over Fourth Like It Means Something
columns.dek: Fourth against fifth, a 3.16-point projected gap and a 52-48 coin flip. Elsewhere, Kris gets Jared, and Brad needs a miracle against a team he owns.
body: The game of the week is Joe G against Jon, because it is fourth against fifth, back to back in the standings, with a playoff spot riding on it. Joe G is fourth at 10-6 with a 80.13% playoff chance; Jon is fifth at 9-7 at 52.55%, which is ESPN's polite way of saying coin flip. The projection agrees: Joe G at 105.05, Jon at 101.89, a gap of 3.16 and a 52% to 48% split. Joe G has won two straight, Jon has lost two, and Joe G leads the series 3-2. Jon is the underdog in a game he can't afford to lose, which is a lot of pressure for a man who is already 9-7.

The closest projection on the board is Brad against TJ, separated by 1.67: TJ at 103.3, Brad at 101.63, 51% to 49%. TJ is third at 10-6, tied on record with Joe G and ahead on points with 842.12. Brad is tenth at 6-10 with an 18.8% playoff chance and has lost two in a row. He also leads this series 5-1, which means TJ has lost five of six to a guy who is now 6-10. Brad needs it far more. TJ needs it a little, and should be embarrassed either way.

The biggest mismatch is Kris against Jared: 98.39 projected against 69.71, a 28.68-point gap and a 31% win chance for Jared. Kris is second at 11-5 and has won two straight. Jared is alone in last at 3-13, has lost four straight, and carries a 1.58% playoff chance. Kris leads the series 9-5. ESPN's projection for Jared reads like a lineup set during a power outage.

Chad, alone in first at 12-4 with a 97.13% playoff chance, is projected for 118.45, the best number on the board, against Jeff's 109.34. That still only makes him a 55% favorite, which is ESPN admitting it has no idea what it's doing. Chad leads the series 12-8. Jeff has lost two straight and is one of three 8-8 teams sitting sixth through eighth.

Those 8-8 teams are the playoff picture. Joe K sits sixth with the worst odds of the three at 43.28%; Ben is at 51.03% and Jeff at 50.13%. Joe K is a 56% favorite over Collin, 101.33 to 91.05, and has won two straight, yet Collin leads that series 6-4. Collin is 4-12 with a 2.7% playoff chance, so losing to him again would take real effort. Ben gets Flanders at 106.13 to 101.76, a 52% favorite against a man who leads the series 11-5. Flanders is ninth at 7-9 with a 35.2% chance, which is a lot of ownership of one man and not much of anyone else.

columns.headline: Chad Hangs 133.68 on Jeff While Jared Starts a Ghost at QB
columns.dek: Chad posts the week's high score with nothing left on the bench, Jared loses a game his own roster could have won, and Brad wins with the seventh-best score in the league.
body: Chad put up 133.68, the high score of the week, and beat Jeff by 60.32, the biggest margin on the board. The annoying part is that there was nothing to second-guess: his best possible lineup was 133.68 too, with zero points left on the bench. Christian Watson did 26.60 against a 12.85 projection, Chad sits alone in first at 14-4, and he now leads the series with Jeff 13-8. Jeff, meanwhile, watched C.J. Stroud score 35.36 from his bench while Josh Jacobs gave him 0.50 as a starter. Even Jeff's best lineup, 103.66, would have been run over, so the Stroud thing is just a souvenir.

The worst loss of the week belongs to Jared, the only manager whose own roster could have won. He started Lamar Jackson at quarterback, and Lamar put up a donut on a projection of nothing, which means ESPN told him in writing. Matthew Stafford scored 11.22 on the bench, Jared's best lineup was 79.72, and Kris won with 75.46. That is a loss by choice. Jared is alone in last at 3-15, and Kris now leads that series 10-5.

Kris is not getting a pass for that win either. 75.46 was ninth of 12 and missed the 83.86 median, and Justin Jefferson managed 7.30 on a 15.10 projection. He stays second at 12-6, and he can thank the one opponent who benched a winning lineup for the W.

The closest game went to Collin, who beat Joe K 109.38 to 102.08, a margin of 7.30. It came down to which Love you had: Collin started Jordan Love, who scored 36.18 against a 17.03 projection, the best start of the week; Joe K started Jeremiyah Love in the flex and got a donut. T.J. Hockenson scored 5.30 on Joe K's bench, which is dumb, though Joe K's best lineup of 105.98 still loses, so it was dumb for free. Joe K had the fifth-best score in the league, lost anyway and slid to seventh. Collin leads the series 7-4 and is still 11th at 6-12, so he gets the win and none of the dignity.

Jon beat Joe G 124.10 to 88.58 and jumped two spots to third, behind Kenneth Walker III's 34.30 and a lineup that left nothing on the bench. For once the production budget bought a finished product. Joe G left Kayshon Boutte and his 26.50 on the bench, on a 3.69 projection, while Aaron Jones Sr. gave him 2.60 in the flex. Little brother Chad left zero points on his bench this week; big brother left 25.50. The series is tied 3-3, and Joe G and Jon are both 11-7, with Jon ahead on points.

TJ posted the low score, 63.14, and lost to Brad, whose 79.14 was seventh in the week and below the median. TJ started Ladd McConkey in the flex for a donut while Jadarian Price scored 9.80 on the bench, though his best lineup of 77.34 still loses to a Brad team that got a donut at tight end from Mason Taylor. TJ fell two spots to fifth; Brad climbed to ninth and leads that series 6-1. Brad would like it noted that his head is not that big, which tracks with a win this small.

Ben handled Flanders 110.04 to 75.50 behind Joe Burrow's 29.54 and moved up to sixth, even with Adonai Mitchell's flex donut and KC Concepcion's 16.80 on the bench. Flanders started Jared Goff for 5.30 on a 19.41 projection while Caleb Williams scored 12.76 on the bench, and Samaje Perine added a donut. Even the best version only reaches 85.46, so it was not close. Flanders still leads the series 11-6 and dropped to tenth at 7-11, tied with Brad on record.

columns.headline: Jon and Kris Meet at 9-5 With the Series Dead Even
columns.dek: Third against fourth, tied 3-3 all time, and ESPN can only split it 52-48. Elsewhere, Chad gets a projected layup and Jared gets a reminder of what 3-11 looks like.
body: The game of the week is Jon against Kris, and it picks itself. Both sit at 9-5, Jon third and Kris fourth, the all-time series is tied 3-3, and ESPN projects Jon at 105.48 to Kris at 102.62, a 52% to 48% coin flip with a gap of 2.86. Jon is coming off a loss, Kris off a win, and both are part of a four-way 9-5 logjam behind Chad. Jon will presumably cut a hype video for this one. The lighting will be immaculate and the lineup will be projected for 105.48.

The tightest projection on the board actually belongs to Ben and Joe G, separated by 2.62. Ben is 6-8, tenth, and somehow ESPN's favorite at 52%. He also owns this series 11-4. Joe G is 9-5 with a 73.98% playoff chance, better than Jon's or Kris's, while his little brother Chad sits alone in first at 10-4. The older brother is supposed to know better, and he is a game behind the kid and projected to lose to a 6-8 team.

The biggest mismatch is Joe K against Chad: 82.72 projected against 116.00, a 33.28 gap and a 31% win chance. Joe K leads the series 10-6, which is the only number on this page that likes him. Chad has 852.0 points this season and a 93% playoff chance; Joe K has a projection that reads like a bye week and a 7-7 record to match.

Streaks: TJ has won three straight and gets Flanders, who has won two, with ESPN giving TJ 63% and a 104.63 to 84.70 edge. TJ leads that series 4-1, so Flanders's hot streak is walking into a wall. At the bottom, Collin has lost four in a row and Jared three. Jared leads Jeff 16-7 all time, a fun fact for a man projected at 84.95 with a 6.95% playoff chance against Jeff's 109.47.

The playoff picture is getting crowded in the middle. Jeff, Flanders and Joe K are all 7-7, and Jeff has the best odds of the three at 51.25%. Brad and Ben are 6-8 at 29.2% and 34.53%. Collin is 2-12 with a 0.75% playoff chance, and he draws Brad, a 53% favorite at 97.08 to 91.85. Brad leads that series 6-4 and needs this one badly. Losing it to the last-place team would be a hell of a way to find out his head really is that big.

columns.headline: Joe K Benches a Win Against Chad, Who Was Very Grateful
columns.dek: Chad survived the closest game of the week by 3.36 because Joe K left a winning lineup on the bench. Kris put up the high score and Jared started a donut at quarterback.
body: The closest game of the week was decided on Joe K's bench. Chad beat him 125.50 to 122.14, a 3.36-point margin, and Joe K was the only loser in the league whose best lineup would have won. That lineup was 133.64. He benched T.J. Hockenson and his 13.80 and started Jeremiyah Love in the flex, who returned 2.30 on a 10.34 projection. That is 11.50 points left on the pine in a game lost by 3.36, which is dumb, and the league has already approved the word. Patrick Mahomes gave him 25.44 on a 14.23 projection and he wasted it. Joe K still beat the 104.83 median, climbed to sixth at 8-8, and leads the series 10-7, which will be no comfort at all.

Chad, meanwhile, got away with it. Jahmyr Gibbs scored 23.80, Bucky Irving added 21.00, and Chad is alone in first at 12-4 with 977.50 points. The margin that kept him there was gift-wrapped by Joe K's flex.

Kris put up the high score of the week, 129.16, and used it on Jon, who managed 68.70. The 60.46-point margin was the biggest of the week, and Kris now leads that series 4-3. Tony Pollard scored 27.20 on a 13.84 projection and Kris jumped two spots to second at 11-5. Jon benched Emmett Johnson, who scored 22.80, and started Parker Washington in the flex for 3.10 on a 13.88 projection. His best lineup of 104.80 would still have lost, so it only made it uglier. Jon spends real money making weekly videos; this week's footage is 68.70 points of a man falling from third to fifth at 9-7. Gorgeous production, terrible product.

Jared posted the low score of the week, 46.30, and the reason starts at quarterback: Lamar Jackson put up a donut on a 22.17 projection. His best lineup was 66.58, so even the bench couldn't have caught Jeff's 95.18, and Jared sits alone in last at 3-13. Jeff took the win and still missed the median, because Drake London gave him 1.30 on a 14.82 projection and Josh Downs laid a donut in the flex. Jared still leads that series 16-8, which is nice for him.

The best start of the week against projection went to Collin: Tee Higgins scored 32.50 on a 13.00 projection, beating it by 19.50, and Collin beat Brad 127.02 to 75.66. That was the second-best score of the week and it moved Collin up out of last to 11th at 4-12. Brad got 28.90 from Bhayshul Tuten, 4.70 from Jonathan Taylor on a 14.31 projection, and a donut from Roschon Johnson at running back. His entire bench scored nothing, so nothing on the bench would have saved him. Brad falls to tenth at 6-10, still leads the series 6-5, and would like everyone to know his head is not that big, which is the one thing about his team this week that isn't small.

Ben had the best possible lineup of anyone at 163.88 and still only scored 121.28, because Tyler Allgeier scored 33.60 on his bench while Javonte Williams started for 6.20 on a 19.11 projection and J.K. Dobbins added 1.30. He left 42.60 on the bench and beat Joe G anyway, with Joe Burrow putting up 39.48. Ben leads that series 12-4 and jumped three spots to seventh at 8-8. Joe G got 28.18 from Kirk Cousins and a donut from Zay Flowers on a 16.69 projection, lost by 6.80, beat the median, and somehow moved up to fourth at 10-6.

TJ beat Flanders 88.76 to 51.18 and leads that series 5-1, but 88.76 missed the median and he slid to third at 10-6, tied on record with Joe G and ahead on points. He started Tre Tucker in the flex for a donut and benched Brian Thomas Jr., who scored 7.70. It didn't matter, which is the only reason it isn't the dumbest thing in this column. Flanders got a donut from Omar Cooper Jr. in the flex, 13.98 from Caleb Williams as his top scorer, and fell three spots to ninth at 7-9.

columns.headline: Chad vs Brad: 20 Meetings, Dead Even, Somebody Finally Blinks
columns.dek: The all-time series is tied 10-10, Chad has the league's biggest points total, and Brad is riding a three-game heater. ESPN likes Chad. Brad likes Brad.
body: The game of the week is Chad against Brad, and it isn't close as a choice. The all-time series is tied 10-10, which means twenty meetings have settled exactly nothing. Chad sits second at 8-4 with 744.8 points for, the biggest pile in the league, and a playoff chance of 87.65%. Brad is 6-6, seventh, on a W3 streak, and sitting at 43.48%, which is fantasy for "we'll see."

ESPN projects Chad at 118.01 to Brad's 98.4 and gives Chad a 60% win chance. That's the projection talking, not the verdict, and Brad will tell you the number undersells him the same way he insists his head isn't that big. Win this and the series finally has a leader. Lose it and Brad's heater goes back in the drawer with the rest of his 6-6 season.

The closest projection on the board is Jon against Ben, a gap of 0.99 with ESPN calling it 51% to 49%. Jon is first at 9-3 and projected for 102.86; Ben is tenth at 5-7 and projected for 101.87. So the league leader, the man with the most expensive weekly video budget in fantasy history, is projected to beat a 5-7 team by less than a point. Great production values, coin-flip product. Jon leads the series 3-2.

The biggest mismatch is Jared against Joe K, a projected gap of 22.65. Joe K is projected for 105.13 and a 64% win chance, which is ESPN trusting Joe K with something, a bold choice. Jared is 3-9, on an L2 skid, projected for 82.48, and staring at a 15.13% playoff chance. Joe K leads that series 13-7, so if Jared loses this one too, it's tradition, not news. If Joe K blows it, that's a whole different column.

Kris and Jeff are both 7-5 and both live in the playoff bubble, Kris fourth and Jeff sixth. ESPN has Jeff at 91.4 to Kris's 88.39, a 52% to 48% lean, and Jeff brings a W2 streak against Kris's L1. Kris leads the series 9-5 and has the points edge, 613.76 to 567.94, but neither of them is projected to clear the projected median of 100.01. Somebody wins ugly.

Joe G gets TJ, who is 8-4 and third. Joe G is projected for 101.98 and a 55% chance despite an L2 streak, and he leads the series 4-2. Down at the bottom, Collin is 2-10, alone in last, on an L3 run with a 4.35% playoff chance. ESPN still makes him a 51% favorite over Flanders, 100.66 to 99.35, which is either a sign of life or a projection system with a sense of humor. Flanders leads that series 9-5.

columns.headline: TJ Benches His Way Out of a Win as Chad Takes First Alone
columns.dek: TJ's best lineup beat Joe G and he didn't play it. Chad hung 49.38 on Brad and owns first place by himself. Jon fell off the top.
body: The week's closest game was also its dumbest. Joe G beat TJ 108.62 to 105.64, a 2.98-point margin, and TJ was the only loser in the league whose best lineup would have won. That lineup was 108.84. He left Tyrone Tracy Jr. on the bench with 8.20 and started Derrick Henry at running back, who returned 5.40 on a 17.37 projection. That is 3.20 points left on the pine in a game decided by less, which is dumb, plain and simple, and the league has signed off on the word.

The insult is that TJ still climbed. Drake Maye's 27.44 and Jaxon Smith-Njigba's 26.80 cleared the 101.55 median by 4.09, so he banked the side win and moved from third to second at 9-5, ahead of a three-way pile at the same record on points. Joe G leads that series 5-2 and gets no credit here either: Brock Purdy scored 12.02 on a 20.43 projection and Aaron Jones Sr. gave him 3.10 in the flex. Zay Flowers and his 23.70 did the rest, and Joe G sits fifth at 9-5.

The biggest beating belonged to Chad, who took Brad apart 107.20 to 57.82, a 49.38-point margin. Brad's 57.82 was the low score of the week by a mile, Bryce Young delivered 5.42 on a 17.66 projection, and Roschon Johnson added 1.30. His best lineup was 68.12, so there was no bench move hiding in there, just a bad roster having a bad day. Brad drops from seventh to ninth at 6-8, and Chad now leads the series 11-10. Chad, meanwhile, got 23.50 from Bucky Irving and 21.70 from Luther Burden III, survived Nico Collins scoring 1.60 on a 14.01 projection, and is alone in first at 10-4 with 852.00 points.

That top spot came at Jon's expense. Jon lost to Ben 96.08 to 85.28, finished 11th of 12 to miss the median too, and went 0-2 on the week, sliding from first to third. Kenneth Walker III scored 7.70 on a 17.74 projection in the flex and Juwan Johnson added 1.20 at tight end; even Jon's best lineup of 89.18 would have lost. Ben will take the win and the 3-3 series tie, but his 96.08 was still under the median, so he went 1-1 and stays tenth. Joe Burrow's 28.88 did the lifting while Jalen Coker gave him 1.40 on a 12.57 projection.

Flanders put up the high score of the week, 115.82, beat Collin, and jumped from eighth to sixth. He also had the best possible lineup of anyone at 137.82, because Omar Cooper Jr. scored 20.00 on his bench while Germie Bernard started at receiver for 4.20. He left 22.00 on the bench and won anyway, which is the most expensive way to win a fantasy game. Cam Skattebo's 18.60 on a 7.32 projection helped cover it. Collin got 23.80 from Tee Higgins and a donut at receiver from Garrett Wilson, started the best lineup he had, and still sits alone in last at 2-12. Flanders leads that series 10-5.

Joe K beat Jared 114.20 to 86.40, the second-best score of the week, and climbed from ninth to seventh. He did it while being dumb: Keon Coleman, projected for nothing, started in the flex and laid exactly the donut he was projected for, while Devaughn Vele scored 13.90 on the bench. Jameson Williams bailed him out with 23.60 on an 8.95 projection, which made Patrick Mahomes and his 6.00 survivable. Jared got a donut from Rashid Shaheed at receiver, but his entire bench scored nothing, so nothing on the bench would have saved him. He stays 11th at 3-11, and Joe K leads that series 14-7.

The best start of the week against projection went to Kris: Tony Pollard scored 35.00 on a 12.92 projection, beating it by 22.08, and Kris beat Jeff 110.62 to 92.72 to hold fourth at 9-5. He left Emanuel Wilson's 18.00 on the bench and won by 17.90, so nobody will ask. Jeff started George Kittle in the flex for a donut on a 13.95 projection and Terry McLaurin at receiver, projected for nothing, for another donut. Trey McBride's 22.10 could only do so much, his best lineup of 95.92 still lost, and Jeff falls from sixth to eighth. Kris leads that series 10-5.

columns.headline: Jon Loses His Way Into First as Brad Hangs 147.14 on Jared
columns.dek: Brad had the high score and the biggest beating, Kris lost by a hair with the winning lineup on his own bench, and Jon took first place with a loss.
body: Brad dropped 147.14 on Jared, the high score of the week and the biggest beating, a 69.76-point margin that stretches his series lead to 15-4. Bhayshul Tuten scored 22.70 on an 11.69 projection, and Brad's best possible lineup was 150.04, and he left only 2.90 on the bench. It moved him up exactly one spot, to seventh at 6-6, which tells you everything about the five weeks before it. Brad has always insisted his head isn't that big and his dick isn't that small, and a score like this does more for the second claim than the first. Jared took the other end of it: Bijan Robinson scored 6.30 on a 21.34 projection, Tyjae Spears added 1.30, and Kyle Pitts Sr.'s 20.50 was a lifeboat on a sunk ship. He falls two spots to 11th at 3-9.

Jon lost to TJ 101.60 to 95.42 and still took sole possession of first place at 9-3, because 95.42 cleared the 83.65 median and banked a win on the side. Kenneth Walker III scored 26.90 and DeVonta Smith 17.00, while Juwan Johnson at tight end and Antonio Williams at receiver each put up a donut. A big production budget, two blank frames, and a premiere that somehow lands in first place: that is the Jon video model in one week. TJ's win ran on Tre Tucker's 24.20 against an 8.59 projection, the best start of the week against projection, which covered for Derrick Henry's 4.50 on a 17.60 projection. TJ climbs to third at 8-4, and Jon still leads the series 5-2.

The closest game was Ben 83.72, Kris 82.10, a 1.62-point margin, and Kris has nobody to blame but Kris. His best lineup was 88.30, enough to win, and it left Woody Marks and his 9.10 on the bench while Rhamondre Stevenson took the flex for 3.60. Falling short of the median meant he lost twice in one afternoon. He slides from third to fourth and Ben takes the series lead, 9-7. Ben cleared the median by 0.07, which is not a victory so much as an administrative error in his favor.

Joe K missed that same median by 0.07, then lost to Jeff 100.30 to 83.58 and fell from seventh to ninth at 5-7. He did start the best lineup he had, so the blame goes to Patrick Mahomes, who scored 10.48 against an 18.77 projection, and to a roster where only Matthew Golden's 19.40 showed up for work. Jeff won while doing his best to give it away: C.J. Stroud scored 22.98 on his bench, Terry McLaurin started at receiver for 3.20 while Jakobi Meyers sat with 10.80, and Jeff left 15.48 behind and still won by 16.72. He leads that series 12-8.

Chad started the week in first place and finished it in second, losing to Flanders 104.50 to 83.24 despite 27.34 from Trevor Lawrence. Kyren Williams scored 8.20 on a 19.17 projection, Wan'Dale Robinson added 3.70 in the flex, and even Chad's best lineup of 92.94 would have lost, so there is no bench to blame. His 744.80 points lead the league, which makes him the highest-scoring team in the league and somehow not first in it. Flanders posted the second-best score of the week, jumped three spots to eighth, and got 20.20 from Germie Bernard against a 7.79 projection, despite Will Shipley laying a donut in the flex. Chad still leads that series 12-10.

Joe G beat Collin 78.66 to 69.14 with the tenth-best score of the week, below the median, with Mark Andrews adding 0.90 in the flex and Harold Fannin Jr. 1.40 at tight end. It is a win, it is 7-5, and it is fifth place, and it looks like a clerical error. Collin took the low score of the week and sits last at 2-10. He started Jordan Love for 20.24 while Tyler Shough scored 26.96 on the bench, but his best lineup of 77.16 would have lost anyway, so that is a footnote to a bad roster, not the story. Joe G leads that series 9-6.

columns.headline: Chad Flattens Joe G and Takes Over First Place
columns.dek: Chad posted the week's best score by a mile, Jon won with the tenth-best score and still slid out of first, and Collin left a winning quarterback on the bench.
body: Chad did not so much beat Joe G as file a noise complaint against him. The final was 155.24 to 68.26, a margin of 86.98, the highest and lowest scores of the week in the same box. Jahmyr Gibbs put up 35.20 and Christian Watson beat his projection by 17.78. The series now sits tied 11-11, and Chad leads the standings at 8-2, ahead of Jon on points. Even his worst lineup call was a rounding error: 1.40 points left on the bench.

Joe G, meanwhile, got 1.90 from CeeDee Lamb on a 15.46 projection, and RJ Harvey chipped in 0.70. His best possible lineup was 81.36, so no bench move was saving this one. He drops from third to fifth at 6-4, which is still a winning record, which is the nicest thing anyone can say about his Sunday.

Now the one that hurts. Collin lost the week's closest game to Jon, 81.54 to 74.42, by 7.12. He started Tyler Shough at quarterback, who finished at -0.16 on a 16.51 projection, while Jordan Love sat on his bench with 25.28. Collin's best lineup was 107.46, enough to win, which makes him the only loser this week who chose his loss. He left 33.04 on the pine and slides to last at 2-8.

Jon will take the win, and he should, because it was a heist. His 81.54 was tenth of 12, well under the 100.25 median, and his bench produced exactly 0.00. Parker Washington's 27.40 carried the lineup. Jon went 1-1 on the week, and he slid from first to second at 8-2, behind Chad on points. Jon leads that series 4-3.

Jeff beat Brad 108.36 to 100.70 despite starting a quarterback who scored 0.00 on an 18.17 projection, with C.J. Stroud and his 20.94 sitting on the bench. Jayden Daniels and his 32.26 covered for it. Jeff jumps from ninth to sixth. Brad got 26.90 from Isaiah Likely and 1.10 from Carnell Tate, beat the 100.25 median by 0.45, and still lost. He stays eighth and still leads Jeff 10-7 in the series, for what that is worth this week.

TJ owns the start of the week: Drake Maye put up 39.46 on an 18.47 projection, beating it by 20.99, and TJ beat Ben 123.56 to 99.80. Ben missed the median by 0.45, got 1.10 from David Montgomery, and fell from seventh to tenth. Joe K handled Kris 124.88 to 105.50 and climbed from tenth to seventh. Kris left MarShawn Lloyd's 16.20 on the bench, but his best lineup was 124.00, still short, so blame the opponent and not the clipboard.

Down in the cellar, Flanders beat Jared 96.34 to 85.92 while getting 0.00 from tight end Kenyon Sadiq, and that was enough to climb out of last to eleventh. Jared got 1.50 from Deebo Samuel Sr. and fell from sixth to ninth. Jared still leads that series 9-8.
